source_title: Growth and Culture: Jorgen Vig Knudstorp Interview
publisher_issuer: Boston Consulting Group (interview with LEGO chairman/former CEO; corroborated by named reporting)
company_context: The LEGO Group, the Danish toy manufacturer, neared bankruptcy in 2003-2004 after years of over-diversification into theme parks, clothing, video games, and media that eroded margins and burned cash. In 2004 Jorgen Vig Knudstorp, a former McKinsey consultant, became CEO and led a return-to-core-brick turnaround.
evidence_summary: By 2003 LEGO was in financial crisis: sales had fallen sharply (reported around 26-30% over a short span) and the company reported a large net loss for the year (widely reported as roughly DKK 1.4 billion / about $300 million) with heavy debt and negative cash flow, raising bankruptcy risk within ~18 months. Root cause was over-diversification away from the core brick system into parks, apparel, games, and media. Knudstorp (CEO from 2004) cut SKUs roughly from 13,000 to 7,000, exited unprofitable ventures (sold theme parks to what became Merlin Entertainments; wound down in-house video games), and refocused on the core brick system, restoring profitability and growth.
outcome_evidence: Under Knudstorp from 2004 LEGO pruned product lines, exited diversified ventures, and returned to its core brick system, executing one of the most cited corporate turnarounds and growing into a multi-billion-dollar profitable company (outcome 4). Crisis phase reflects margin_erosion/over-diversification.
source_limitations: Specific loss figures (DKK 1.4B / ~$300M) and sales-decline percentages are drawn from secondary case-study and reporting snippets, not a fetched LEGO annual report; LEGO is private, so primary filings are limited. The qualitative turnaround and Knudstorp's 2004 appointment are well corroborated. Treated as B and figures flagged as approximate/'reported as'.
directly_stated: 2003 financial crisis with large annual loss (reported ~DKK 1.4 billion / ~$300 million)
sharp sales decline over a short span
over-diversification into parks/clothing/games/media as root cause
SKU count cut from about 13,000 to 7,000
exited theme parks and in-house video games
inferred: diversification destroyed margin and focus while core brand equity remained intact
narrowing scope back to core was the corrective lever enabling recovery
why_useful_for_opsiq: Margin-erosion / over-diversification crisis corrected by disciplined scope reduction back to core, producing a durable turnaround. Tests OpsIQ's diagnosis of margin_erosion vs cash crisis, and re-evaluation triggered by a major scope change (strategic refocus).
